standard_prerequisites: Rational equivalence on cycles on a good algebraic space: cycles of dimension k are equivalent when their difference is a locally finite sum of divisors of rational functions on integral closed subspaces of dimension k plus one
Proper pushforward of cycles, its compatibility with composition of proper morphisms, and the scheme theoretic image of a proper morphism applied to an integral closed subspace

The scheme case of the statement and the alteration lemma for proper pushforward when the image has the same dimension, together with the criterion identifying a one-dimensional fibre over a generic point with a scheme
core_obligations: Unwind rational equivalence: given a locally finite family of closed immersions of integral subspaces of dimension k plus one with rational functions, show that the proper pushforward of the sum of their divisors is rationally equivalent to zero

Rewrite the pushforward of the sum as the sum of the pushforwards of the individual divisors, replace each image by the scheme theoretic image of the composite morphism, and note that the images form a locally finite family so that it suffices to handle one closed immersion at a time

Reduce further to a single integral closed subspace W of X of dimension k plus one with a rational function f and its image W' in Y, and use compatibility of pushforward with composition to reduce the claim to the statement that the pushforward of the divisor of f to W' is zero or is the divisor of a rational function
Case image of dimension less than k: the pushed forward cycle has dimension below k, hence vanishes automatically

Case image of dimension k: the pushforward is an integer multiple of the class of W', so it suffices to show the integer is zero; shrink W' to be a scheme, base change along the generic point of W' to get a one-dimensional proper cover of the spectrum of the function field, identify it as a scheme via the codimension one criterion and a limit argument, and invoke the scheme case
Case image of dimension k plus one: apply the alteration lemma to exhibit the pushforward of the divisor as the divisor of a rational function on the image
proof_roadmap: Translate the claim into a statement about the pushforward of one summand and reduce to an integral closed subspace of dimension k plus one
Set up the commutative square with the image of that subspace and use composition of pushforwards
Settle the cases where the image has dimension less than k or exactly k, the latter by shrinking to a scheme and passing to the generic point
Settle the case where the dimension is preserved by quoting the alteration lemma
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the compatibility of proper pushforward with rational equivalence at source lines 2175-2181, label lemma-proper-pushforward-rational-equivalence, whose proof occupies source lines 2183-2269. The proof reduces a locally finite sum of divisors on integral subspaces to a single summand and then splits into three cases according to the dimension of the image. The dimension-preserving case is disposed of by an alteration lemma, but the case where the image has dimension exactly k requires real work: the pushforward is first seen to be an integer multiple of the image class, then the image is shrunk to a scheme, the generic point is pulled back to a one-dimensional proper cover, that cover is proved to be a scheme through the codimension one criterion for the schematic locus and a limit argument, and only then does the scheme case give vanishing. The counted statement records none of the case distinction.
